runs.content: Monday's rotation focus is Finance + Crypto. Since the last thinker run (2026-09-06), log.md shows only two routine automated updates — the growth-value-tracker and sector-performance-tracker weekly refreshes — with no new clippings or portfolio moves to review. Deep-reading both trackers plus Crypto's overview and portfolio pages surfaced one genuinely new, non-duplicate investigation idea: Ray Dalio's March 2026 piece on the Strait of Hormuz ([[finance/investor-letters/source-dalio-strait-of-hormuz]]) argued, five months ahead of the fact, that control of the Strait would be the single decisive flashpoint of the Iran war. On 2026-08-31 that materialized almost exactly as described — US strikes on Iranian sites, a WTI spike — and the paper-trading book opened a live trade (OXY) explicitly citing the resulting sector tailwind. A grep of the paper-trading trade log turned up five more trades (COP, CMCL, ICE, CMCSA, XOM) independently citing the same Strait-of-Hormuz risk premium as a catalyst across the past several months, none of which cross-link Dalio's own analysis — a real, recurring pattern (his macro framework has been quietly playing out in the simulated book for months) rather than a one-off. Today's sector tracker refresh independently confirms Energy is the tracker's best value/momentum sector this run, reinforcing that the pattern is still live. No new cross-domain connection cleared the bar today (Crypto's BTC recovery to $79.7k and the sector tracker's other moves are continuations of already-logged threads), and nothing in the existing open sections showed clear signs of resolution.

Sunday's rotation focus is 'whichever domain has gone longest without a deep-dive' — Lightfin was chosen (last substantive content added 2026-05-28, only skim-touched on Friday rotations since). Since the last thinker run (2026-09-05), log.md shows only routine automated activity (a Magic Formula ranking update and a portfolio-refresh) with nothing new to cross-reference. Deep-reading Lightfin's overview, story-bible, characters, story-arc, inspiration-authors, adaptation-overview and its sister creative project project-optimised-jungle.md surfaced one genuinely new, non-duplicate cross-domain connection: Tom Slater's real AI-cognitive-decline investment research (ai-tech/source-slater-ai-mind-2026 — 'AI reliably improves immediate task performance while degrading the underlying human capabilities that produce that performance,' with neuroscience on the brain region that atrophies without effortful friction) is almost a line-for-line match for the 'Willing Cage' theme at the heart of Fred's own satirical novel outline, project-optimised-jungle.md ('most animals don't need to be forced... The cage is comfortable. That's the point' — a Pod that removes friction one convenience at a time). The novel's own Inspirations table already credits Orwell/Carlin/Stewart/Galloway/Evans but never Slater's cognition research, despite Fred having read and filed it four months before drafting the outline. No new investigation idea cleared the bar today (Lightfin's existing open threads — finale outlines, the financial-literacy-game crossover, Sound School/Scriptnotes craft gaps — are all already logged), and nothing in the existing open sections showed clear signs of resolution.
